what: MAIN verification of paperC assumption A-03 -- the 6 classical-statistics citations
verified_by: MAIN (not delegated); Crossref CSL-JSON via doi.org, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar
why_this_matters: A-03 is the highest-risk assumption in paperC/state/assumptions.md. Unlike the ICLR/ACL citations, these six are pre-digital works covered by NEITHER family verification file. The paper's contribution IS a measurement rule resting on the psychometric best-constant idea, so this is exactly where a reviewer probes attribution.
IMPORTANT_risk_direction_correction: MAIN re-read the citing sentences before verifying and found the risk runs the OPPOSITE way to what A-03 assumes. All six are cited inside a DISCLAIMER passage (09a_relocated.tex:8 and 03_method.tex:52) whose function is to give ground away: 'We therefore claim NONE of the following: correcting for the number of options, choosing p_e as a methodological decision, or noticing that kappa-family statistics depend on k.' cohen1960kappa at 02_related.tex:15 likewise says the constant-emitter zero 'is that literature's standard property rather than a new result.' So the failure mode is NOT the paper stealing credit. It is the paper (a) conceding ground that may not belong to these works, and (b) drawing its own novelty boundary in the wrong place as a result. A-03 as written says the danger is 'whether the paper is claiming as novel something Frary (1988) already said'. That danger is structurally ABSENT here -- the paper explicitly disclaims Frary's content. The real danger is over-disclaiming.

axis_2_local_support.bennett_abstract_recovered_verbatim: The extent of consistency between information from two methods of communication, the interview and the limited-response question, was investigated. Thirty questions showed consistencies greater than could be expected on the basis of chance. axis_2_local_support.bennett_assessment: INSUFFICIENT to support the paper's specific claim. The paper asserts "Bennett's S sets p_e=1/k for k response categories". Consistent with the claim, does not establish it. MAIN will not upgrade this to VERIFIED on an abstract.

MAIN_INDEPENDENT_CHECK_1430.what: MAIN re-fetched the Brennan & Prediger 1981 abstract itself via OpenAlex rather than trusting the agent's quotation
MAIN_INDEPENDENT_CHECK_1430.verbatim_confirmed: In validity studies, we suggest considering whether one wants an index of improvement beyond "chance" or beyond the best a priori strategy employing base rates. In the former case, considerations are similar to those in reliability studies with the marginals for the criterion measure considered as fixed. In the latter case, it is suggested that the largest marginal proportion for the criterion measure be used in place of the "chance" term in kappa.
MAIN_INDEPENDENT_CHECK_1430.verdict: The agent's central finding is CORRECT and MAIN verified it from the source, not from the agent's report. This sentence is paperC's v1 floor: f_const = max_L (1/n) sum 1[y_i = L] is the largest gold-label marginal used in place of chance. The criterion measure is the gold label (one correct answer per item), so the correspondence is exact, and even the chance-vs-best-a-priori framing matches the paper's own introduction.
MAIN_INDEPENDENT_CHECK_1430.attribution_gap: brennan1981kappa appears exactly twice in the manuscript, both inside the v2 paragraph disclaiming the 1/k choice. v1 -- the paper's flagship, which it does NOT disclaim -- credits only the ML-side balepur2024artifacts. So the paper cites this work for the lesser of its two recommendations and misses the one that is its own headline's direct antecedent.
MAIN_INDEPENDENT_CHECK_1430.this_is_a_NET_GAIN_not_a_defect: Not plagiarism: the paper never claims the statistic is new. But an uncited antecedent INSIDE AN ALREADY-CITED reference is a real attribution gap a reviewer will hit on opening a 1502-citation classic already in the bibliography. Handled correctly it UPGRADES the paper: v1 stops being an ad-hoc ML heuristic and becomes a 1981 psychometric recommendation with a citation -- which is exactly the repair X1 asked for when it wrote that the 'boundary against the closest work is incomplete'. The edit is ADDITIVE (one sentence), removing nothing.
MAIN_INDEPENDENT_CHECK_1430.risk_direction_prediction_CONFIRMED: MAIN predicted at 13:20 that A-03's stated failure mode was backwards -- that the risk was over-disclaiming, not over-claiming. All three PARTIALLY_SUPPORTED verdicts are over-disclaiming, and all four recommended edits ADD precision and favour the paper. The prediction held.
